correctness.rationale: Faithfulness makes every singular competitor have infinite divergence; the diagonal state at reward τ is finite. For a feasible faithful competitor above τ, mixing toward ρ until reward equals τ strictly lowers D by convexity and D(ρ||σ)>0. On the boundary, spectral calculus gives log σ=(1/2)log[(1−q²)/4]·I+(artanh q/q)s·σ_Pauli. At a nonzero transverse radius, p>0 makes the azimuth aligned with the arm uniquely optimal; at radius zero the azimuth does not distinguish states. Substituting the aligned vector gives the claimed D and differentiation gives D′. Along this affine line the second derivative is 2∫Tr(ρ BHBHB)du>0, with B=(σ+uI)⁻¹ and H=σ_x/2, by the integral representation of −log and ρ>0. At zero radius D′(0)=−p·artanh(|z|)/|z|<0, continued to −p at z=0. At the positive pure-state endpoint the positive (1−q²)⁻¹ term dominates the logarithmic term, since the arm Bloch norm is strictly less than one. Hence there is exactly one interior root and global minimizer. Independent 60-digit bisection gave x*=0.2559243261276990811, D_inf=1.1173300547617507845, K_inf=0.8303656034108254540 and 1−K_inf/D_inf=0.2568305131755495459, agreeing with the published rounding in the frozen result. Ng's running parameters and converse were checked against the primary text. The bundled artifacts/verify.py was inspected, not executed; the reproduction supplements the proof. The percentage bounds a potential coefficient reduction, not an attainable operational improvement.
